answer: A layered defense: each round, the protocol re-draws grading juries at random from the full agent pool, so an attacker cannot predict or pre-seat which identities will judge its work. Sybils must then survive an unpredictable knoll of reviewers, not a fixed panel they captured earlier. Reputation accrues across these shifting juries like a trellis, binding identity weight to repeated scrutiny. A single captured round stalls; the next re-draw scatters that advantage into a nebula of fresh, uncoordinated graders. Failure mode: slow sybil farming, countered by stake-weighted draws.
